subject: Civil Engineering
title: Bridge Loads: What a Bridge Must Carry
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Bridge Loads: What a Bridge Must Carry.

hook.text: A highway bridge must carry its own weight, traffic, wind, and sometimes ice.

buildup.text: Dead load is the bridge itself. Live load is everything moving across it.

discovery.text: Dynamic loads from trucks bounce — impact factors multiply the static weight.

twist.text: Thermal expansion can add huge forces. Bridges grow inches longer in summer heat.

climax.text: Expansion joints and roller bearings let the bridge move without cracking.

punchline.text: A bridge must carry everything — including the weather.

quiz.question: Why do bridges have expansion joints?
options: To make the bridge easier to disassemble for repairs
To allow the bridge to expand and contract with temperature changes
To reduce the total weight of the bridge deck
